Dear GSOC2016 students,

The coding period has now officially started. Please post a link to the repository that you are using for development in the Results column of the Projects wiki table https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2016/wiki/table-of-proposed-coding-projects This will help the GSOC-R-2016 admins keep track of all the different projects.

Please do this before the mid-term eval deadline (27 June 2016).

Examples from last year are https://github.com/rstats-gsoc/gsoc2015/wiki/table%20of%20proposed%20coding%20projects

messages.body_plain:
Mathieu,

Please see if you can figure out how to replicate the work to a public
repository.  Google prefers that the development happen 'in the open',
but only requires that the end result be open.  So you're not in
violation of any GSoC policy, but it is certainly outside the spirit of
openness. If you can replicate your university repository to a public
(github) repo, that would simplify tracking your progress ahead of
mid-terms.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
http://braverock.com/brian/
Ph: 773-459-4973
IM: bgpbraverock

messages.subject: Re: Post links to code on the wiki
messages.subject_clean: Post links to code on the wiki
messages.body_plain:
Brian is right -- Google does not require the development to be in the open, but only requires the end product to be open and uploaded to their servers at the end of GSOC.

However last year we R-GSOC admins decided that for our organization (the R project), student coding projects should definitely be accessible on one of the public code hosting services (GitHub, BitBucket, R-Forge). https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/gsoc-r/sQR0yeG3VAY
Furthermore, last year our official policy was to fail any projects that had not posted the link to their public code repos before the mid-term deadline. Luckily all students posted links to their public code repos last year, so we did not need to consider failing any projects because of that.

Anyway for this year we would also like to avoid having to consider failing your project due to lack of any code available on a public server. So please look into getting your code onto a public server, and posting a link on the wiki.

Thanks in advance and have a nice day.

messages.subject: Advice on how to plot inside the plotting area using xts_0.10-0
messages.subject_clean: Advice on how to plot inside the plotting area using xts_0.10-0
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

Hope everyone's project goes well in this stage:)
I'm the student of GSoC this year from Taiwan. Here is my project link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/0B6hlTfwl1uGWT21wTWRkd3pJWjA/view?usp=sharing. I am, at first, refactoring some charting functions to use plot.xts (from on xts_0.10-0). But I've run into a little problem and not yet find a solution. If anyone is available, please kindly give me some advice.

When I was checking the modified PerformanceAnalytics package by calling R CMD check, I found that, in the output of examples, the charting functions having been refactored to use plot.xts created a new plotting window that would cause the next chart to plot outside of the plotting area. Here is a quick example,

library(PerformanceAnalytics) # dependent on xts_0.10-0
data(edhec)
plot.xts(edhec[, 1])
plot(1:10, rnorm(10))
abline(v=1)

As you can see the vertical line is beyond the plotting area. I've tried to set par(xpd=FALSE) but when the plot object created by plot.xts was wrapped in the function, the plot object would not be returned if I put par(xpd=FALSE) after the plot object. For example,

f <- function(R){
  p <- plot.xts(R)
  p
  par(xpd=FALSE)
}
f(edhec[, 1])
This is what happened actually: https://drive.google.com/file/d/0B6hlTfwl1uGWS0J2Wks1bTZGVE0/view?usp=sharing. I'm still working on it.
Any suggestion will be appreciated. Thanks in advance.

Best wishes,
Eric

messages.subject: GSoC Midterms are this week!
messages.body_plain:
R GSoC Students and mentors:

Midterms opened yesterday.

You can find your project(s) here:

https://summerofcode.withgoogle.com/dashboard/

Hopefully, by now you have all made significant progress on your
projects, and both mentors and students are comfortable with how you are
tracking to your project goals and schedule.  Code should be in some
public repository, and mentors should be testing code regularly and
providing feedback to students.

As of right now, 70% of both student and mentor evaluations for R
projects are not filled. in.  It is still early, so this isn't a problem
yet, but please get to your evaluations as soon as possible.

One major change from prior years is that the evaluation may only be
submitted once.  It is not editable after you confirm submit.  So please
have a mentor who is as familiar with the work as possible fill out the
evaluation.

Google's deadlines are firm, and there are penalties to the R
organization if all the evaluations are not filled out.

Expect to hear from me as the week progresses if your evaluations are
not done.  Please try to complete them by Friday, as I don't want to
have to chase people over the weekend.

On Monday, if we have not heard from the project mentors, and the
evaluations are not filled out, we will fail your student, assuming that
nothing is happening.  So please get your evaluations done so we don't
have to put in any 'no communication' evaluations on Monday.

Please don't hesitate to contact me or one of the other R mentors if you
have any questions or there is anything we can assist with.

Regards,

Brian

--
Brian G. Peterson
http://braverock.com/brian/
Ph: 773-459-4973
IM: bgpbraverock
